players.product: GPU cloud capacity: usage allocations on NVIDIA GPU servers in the AI data centres it operates

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): net sales JPY 33,605 million (up JPY 30,662 million year on year), mainly because service provision in the AI infrastructure business started in September 2025 and the existing businesses were broadly steady or strong. Operating income JPY 3,544 million (prior year: operating loss of JPY 496 million) after covering heavy up-front investment costs for the AI infrastructure business; adjusted EBITDA JPY 4,205 million (prior year: minus JPY 169 million); ordinary income JPY 3,627 million; net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 2,801 million (prior year: net loss of JPY 654 million). Cost of sales JPY 27,208 million, of which server usage fees JPY 25,154 million. By product, AI infrastructure sales were JPY 30,477,329 thousand of JPY 33,605,038 thousand total (retail marketing JPY 1,918,575 thousand; data analysis solutions JPY 1,209,134 thousand). By segment: Domestic external sales JPY 32,468 million (up JPY 30,549 million) and segment profit JPY 5,057 million (prior year JPY 92 million) - management states AI infrastructure sales and profit expanded sharply as service provision went into full swing from the third quarter; Overseas (FollowUP retail analytics, mainly Chile and Colombia) external sales JPY 1,136 million and segment profit JPY 149 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 33,605 million; operating income JPY 3,544 million; adjusted EBITDA JPY 4,205 million; AI infrastructure sales JPY 30,477,329 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Major customer (annual securities report, sales by principal customer): NowNow Japan Co., Ltd. accounted for JPY 30,477,329 thousand, 90.7% of FY2026 (year ended March 2026) net sales, all in the AI infrastructure business (no customer reached 10% of sales in the prior year). The company states it signed three large AI data-center service-use contracts during the year indirectly, through its business partner NowNow Japan, with a customer that is one of the world's largest cloud service providers; the projects progressed and service provision under one of them started in September 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: JPY 30,477,329 thousand; 90.7% of net sales; 3 large AI data-center service contracts

quarterly_data.signal: GPU server purchase (annual securities report): for the AI data centers of its contracted projects, the company signed in July 2025 a sale-and-purchase agreement with GIGA COMPUTING CO., LTD. (New Taipei City, Taiwan) to acquire as fixed assets a set of 625 GPU servers carrying 5,000 NVIDIA B200 GPUs.

GPU server purchase (annual securities report): for the AI data centers of its contracted projects, the company signed in December 2025 a sale-and-purchase agreement with Inventec Corporation (Taipei, Taiwan) to acquire as fixed assets a set of 1,250 GPU servers carrying 10,000 NVIDIA B300 GPUs. Management states its strategy is to secure NVIDIA GPUs, which are in tight supply worldwide, through business alliances with Taiwanese server suppliers, while developing TAIZA, its own algorithm system that optimises the operation of large GPU clusters; its large prospective pipeline for AI data-center services, mainly in Japan and also in Asia and Europe, is growing.

Company forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027, which it calls a phase of further accelerating growth: net sales JPY 162,193 million, operating income JPY 24,815 million, adjusted EBITDA JPY 58,191 million, ordinary income JPY 12,542 million, net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 8,704 million. The forecast includes data-center sales of JPY 158,726 million in total: JPY 79,864 million from the project whose service started in the prior year; the ordered Japan data center No. 1 (JPY 15,943 million) and Australia data center No. 1 (JPY 34,164 million), both scheduled to start phased operation from July; and the high-certainty pipeline of Thailand data center No. 1 (JPY 15,943 million) and the expansion of Australia data center No. 1 (JPY 12,811 million); other existing businesses JPY 3,467 million. The company expects project profit (before interest) of JPY 26,843 million in total from these data-center projects, and will revise the forecast promptly if progress in the large AI infrastructure pipeline requires it.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 162,193 million; operating income JPY 24,815 million; data-center sales JPY 158,726 million; project profit JPY 26,843 million

quarterly_data.signal: Capex and new-facility plans (annual securities report): capital expenditure in the year ended March 2026 was JPY 5,106 million, mainly JPY 4,497 million of equipment for data centers not yet in operation (construction in progress). Planned new facilities at fiscal year-end (data-center equipment and devices): Chiba Prefecture, Japan, JPY 65,000 million (JPY 1,579 million already paid), started July 2025, completion planned August 2026; Thailand, JPY 48,000 million (JPY 2,918 million paid), March 2026 to August 2026; Australia, JPY 97,000 million, March 2026 to August 2026; plus JPY 1,500 million (JPY 1,411 million paid) at headquarters for the operation-optimisation algorithm for large AI GPU clusters, August 2024 to December 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: FY capex JPY 5,106 million; planned data centers: Chiba JPY 65,000 million, Thailand JPY 48,000 million, Australia JPY 97,000 million, completion August 2026

quarterly_data.signal: In June 2025 the company reached a basic agreement with Mathew Hawkins, the largest shareholder and CEO of CUDO Ventures Ltd. (London; service brand CUDO Compute; an NVIDIA Cloud Partner with operating experience in AI cloud stacks and data-center infrastructure), to make CUDO a subsidiary through a capital alliance, and agreed to set up a joint-venture subsidiary with CUDO; as of the annual securities report, discussions were continuing.
